prose.en: Tori breaks uke's balance to the right front corner, places the left leg in front of uke's right foot and, sacrificing his own body to the side, spreads out and uses both hands to draw uke's body still further to the right front corner and throw him.

Image of the technique and the ukemi (breakfall) Tori breaks uke to the right front, steps the left leg out, and throws while sacrificing his body to the side. Uke's cooperation: Uke takes a mae-mawari-ukemi (forward rolling breakfall), pivoting on the right foot. Tori breaks uke to the right front, steps the left leg out, and throws while sacrificing his body to the side. ① Elementary way of applying the technique The elementary form of uki-waza; the red circle marks uke's right foot, the pivot point. Uke, pivoting on the right foot, takes a mae-mawari-ukemi of his own accord.

Tori breaks uke to the left front corner with the tsuri-te and applies the technique as uke pushes back. Apply the technique at the moment when uke, having once been broken to the left front corner by the tsuri-te (lifting hand), pushes back.

heading.en: Faults that are easy to fall into

prose.en: Tori should draw the hikite (pulling hand) out fully, break uke's balance to the front, and throw in that way.
Uke takes a mae-mawari-ukemi of his own accord so that he does not land on his right shoulder.
